parsed.explanation: Weightiest facts: same-sex conduct is criminalised with an unusually broad 2006 extension to non-sexual contact (holding hands, hugging, kissing), so a trans visitor read legally by birth sex with a partner faces imprisonment; government campaigns against LGBTI people since 1995 documented infiltration, detention, beating, killing and rape by authorities and intelligence-service arrests — state-directed hostility (tier 2), though the most recent prosecution in the record is 1998 and counts are unsourced; a 2014 trans-specific bathroom arrest shows police willingness to charge gender expression; no general anti-discrimination protection; censorship law used against LGBTQ people; border treatment, custody placement and current enforcement frequency are open questions, not evidence of safety. Mitigating and documented: the 2014 charge was thrown out with damages won (courts working for a trans person), a 2018 health-ministry handbook guarantees care including transition-relevant services, and a 35-year-old LGBTI organisation provides legal aid and counselling. Amnesty 2024 places the statutory regime in a pattern of escalating legal hostility.
